bib.title: MINT: Evaluating LLMs in Multi-turn Interaction with Tools and Language Feedback

read.skipped: Reference list skimmed only (lineage); everything else read including appendices A-F.

question: How well do LLMs solve tasks over multiple turns when they can use tools (Python code) and receive natural language feedback, and what training choices (SIFT, RLHF) help or hurt?
hypothesis: Single-turn benchmarks neglect tool use and language feedback, so they misrepresent real-world multi-turn use; LLMs should gain from both.
contributions: MINT, a benchmark of 586 instances from 8 repurposed datasets for multi-turn interaction with tools and language feedback
An evaluation framework where LLMs call tools by executing Python code and receive feedback simulated by GPT-4
Evaluation of 20 LLMs (4 closed, 16 open) measuring tool-augmented task-solving, ability to use feedback and ability to give feedback
Findings that SIFT/RLHF generally hurt multi-turn ability and that single-turn rank does not predict multi-turn rank
Human evaluation that GPT-4 feedback is about as helpful as human feedback

method.summary: Eight datasets are filtered to instances needing multi-turn interaction and sub-sampled to 586. The evaluated LLM takes up to k turns, each either executing Python (tools) or proposing a solution (max 2 proposals); an optional GPT-4 (gpt-4-0613) simulated user gives natural language feedback. Success rate at k=1..5 and its change with feedback measure tool and feedback ability.
method.task: multi-turn tool-augmented task solving (reasoning, code generation, ALFWorld decision-making) with simulated user feedback

datasets.name: MINT (re-purposed)
datasets.source: HumanEval 164->45, MBPP 500->91, ALFWorld 134->134, GSM8K 1319->48, HotpotQA 7,405->43, MATH 5,000->100, MMLU 13,985->76, TheoremQA 800->49
datasets.preprocessing: Drop multiple-choice items with <4 options; for MATH and MMLU drop subject classes whose mean gpt-3.5-turbo-0613 turns fall below a threshold (MATH N=100, k=3.5; MMLU N=20, k=2.5); run gpt-3.5-turbo-0613 with k=5, no feedback and drop instances finished within 2 turns; stratified sampling over 16 strata (8 datasets x solved/unsolved by gpt-3.5) with keep proportions alfworld 1, mbpp 0.5, humaneval 0.5, gsm8k 0.2, hotpotqa 0.2, theoremqa 0.2, MMLU 0.1, MATH 0.05; HotpotQA first 500 instances reserved before filtering

other.also_used: for filtering; fixed evaluated model in feedback-provider study

models.name: Vicuna-v1.5 (SIFT)
models.context: inferred: 4,096 tokens, from 'most modern LLMs' context window (4,096 tokens)'

inference.samples: inferred: one trajectory per instance per setting (no repeats, seeds or variance stated)
inference.prompting: System-style instruction asking for <thought>, then <execute> code or <solution>; 1-shot in-context example per task type (with and without feedback variants); reminder 'You have X steps left and Y chances to propose solution left'; max 5 total steps, 2 proposals
inference.retrieval: Reasoning tasks get a wikipedia_search tool; ALFWorld gets 11 action tools; code generation gets only the Python interpreter

parameters.feedback_conditioning: no ground truth by default (gt_solution = NOT GIVEN); dense (every turn) and textual by default

other.cost_per_model: about 100 USD (3M prompt tokens, 100K completion tokens) with gpt-4-0613 feedback at $0.03/1K prompt and $0.06/1K completion

metrics.name: Success Rate SR_k
metrics.definition: percentage of successful task instances when the model may interact up to k turns; micro-averaged across tasks

metrics.name: Delta_tools
metrics.definition: slope b of least-squares regression of SR_k on k (k=1..5), with R2

metrics.name: Delta_feedback
metrics.definition: SR5 with GPT-4 feedback minus SR5 without feedback

baselines: 20 LLMs compared with each other; lazy-user setting (binary 'Your answer is wrong.' after first wrong proposal) is the no-feedback baseline
eval.protocol: Lazy user checks proposals against ground truth; interaction ends on 2 proposals, a correct solution or turn k. Human evaluation: 113 trajectories, annotators A/B write feedback, C/D compare to GPT-4 feedback on helpfulness and human-likeness (Potato interface). No significance tests.

availability.code: https://xingyaoww.github.io/mint-bench (project website); outputs from all LLMs released in code repo

prompts.text: You are a helpful assistant assigned with the task of problem-solving. To achieve this, you will be using an interactive coding environment equipped with a variety of tool functions to assist you throughout the process. At each turn, you should first provide your step-by-step thinking for solving the task. Your thought process should be enclosed using "<thought>" tag ... 1) Interact with a Python programming environment ... enclosed using "<execute>" tag ... 2) Directly provide a solution ... enclosed using "<solution>" tag ... You have {max_total_steps} chances to interact with the environment or propose a solution. You can only propose a solution {max_propose_solution} times. {tool_desc} --- {in_context_example} --- {task_prompt}

You are an expert tasked with evaluating and providing feedback on an assistant's performance. --- Here is an example. Please follow the format as the following expert acts. {in_context_example} --- {tool_desc} {trajectory} Correct solution (please DO NOT disclose the correct solution to the assistant): {gt_solution} Please provide concise and constructive feedback. Remember, your role is similar to a teacher. Rather than giving away the solution or details about the answer, guide the assistant toward understanding how to arrive at the correct answer. Your feedback should focus on enhancing the assistant's ability to think critically and respond accurately. Now provide your feedback. Expert feedback:

prompts.purpose: Format error message returned to the LLM
prompts.text: I don't understand your input. If you want to execute code, please use <execute> YOUR_CODE_HERE </execute>. If you want to give me an answer, please use <solution> YOUR_SOLUTION_HERE </solution>. For example: The answer to the question is <solution> 42 </solution>.

evidence.quote: You can only propose a solution 2 times.

limits: GPT-4 simulated feedback may not cover real human responses or nuanced judgments of human values (Appendix A).
Does not study training on language feedback (left to future work).
Metrics assess outcome only, not the interaction process; repetitive guessing is not penalized.
Tool coverage is narrow (Python, wikipedia search, ALFWorld actions); no web-browsing or OS tasks.
Single run per setting, no seeds, decoding temperature or max tokens stated; no significance tests.
Authors say it is hard to conclude RLHF in general hurts; some SIFT/RLHF drops are confounded by formatting failures and data artifacts (Vicuna backslash-underscore, CodeLlama [PYTHON]).
Subset construction uses gpt-3.5-turbo-0613 to filter, so difficulty is relative to that model; k=5 is capped by a 4,096-token context.
Models are mid-2023 (GPT-4-0613, Claude 1/2, LLaMA-2); results have dated.

terms.definition: a simulated user who provides at most one additional binary feedback ('Your answer is wrong.') during interaction
improvement per additional interaction turn, estimated as the least-squares slope of SR_k on k
